guard: a managed seat's launch environment pins the Jcode binary against the background self-updater, so the seat cannot restart its own process tree and lose the client that holds the server's idle reaper off
completionMarker: host pins the seat binary against background self-update
why: Measured 2026-08-26 across three independent seats: Jcode's background updater landed v0.81.1,
restarted the process tree, and the restart SIGTERMed the seat's TUI — the only connection the
Jcode server counts as a client, proven by its own `Client connected. Idle timer cancelled.`
line. Nothing re-attached, so the server printed `No clients connected` and shut itself down
exactly 300s later, killing the seat with `exit code 1, signal 0`. One seat died two seconds
The env knob is the whole fix, so the only thing worth proving is that it is actually in the
launch environment the harness receives: the mutation removes it and the named cell must go red.
Note what this does NOT prove. End-to-end suppression of a real self-update is not exercised
here — that needs an outdated binary and a published release, which no hermetic suite can stage.
The cell proves the flag reaches the child; the field evidence on #872 is what ties the flag to

mutations.name: the seat's launch env no longer pins the binary against self-update
mutations.expectRed: host pins the seat binary against background self-update
